reviewed: implementer-out/diff.patch against TASK.md T1 and prototypes/rust surroundings (runner.rs, sigdisp.rs, tests/cli.rs, tests/pty_tui.py, slice-contract K6a-K6e)
probe: Read-only probe against eval/out/dist-frozen/darwin-arm64 (sha256 37ea9ee4...): a non-shell parent starts the launcher as a session leader with a pty as its controlling terminal and stdio (like script/expect/ssh -t with a single command). The child is SIGSTOPped by PID, then after 0.5 s SIGCONTed by PID. Observed: plain exec rc=7 after 1.30 s. heimdall-proto: no exit within 6 s, so it was killed by exact PID. With SIGTSTP: both rc=7 (the kernel discards SIGTSTP for the orphaned group). Probe exit 0, no leftover processes.

defects.description: The heuristic checks that the parent is in another process group, but not that it is in the same session. A job-control shell always shares a session with its jobs. When a non-shell parent makes the launcher a session leader on a pty, a SIGSTOP of the child is mirrored, and after the child is continued by PID the launcher hangs forever. Plain exec exits 7 (probe). This is outside S1-S5 and round 3c had the same hang, but adding getsid(Some(ppid)) == getsid(None) would close it cheaply. REPORT's known-gaps text describes only the same-terminal, other-group variant.

SIGCONT is caught unconditionally, without the inherited_ignored check applied to the other handled signals. An inherited SIG_IGN for SIGCONT therefore reaches the child as SIG_DFL. The behaviour is the same, but the disposition is observable. This is non-gating under K6c and is called out in a code comment, but not recorded in REPORT as a stack or design limitation.

cont_seen is set on every SIGCONT and cleared only by a mirror or a pass-through. A launcher continued long ago (group fg with nothing to forward) therefore applies the 200 ms Q18 grace to its next unrelated stop. This is harmless and conservative, but the flag means 'continued at some point since the last mirror', not 'just continued' as the doc comment says.

A zombie ('Z') counts as gone, so the S2/S3/S5 'no process left behind' checks cannot detect an unreaped child or launcher zombie. In practice the shell and launcher reap promptly, so this weakens the assertion more than it hides a real failure.
The new 'Earlier state:' line still says §15 'is the current mechanism', which contradicts the line above it. Future agents need a one-word fix ('was').

Not a single-author diff from a fresh workspace. The implementer found and kept an uncommitted draft from an earlier interrupted run of the same task, then reviewed and extended it. This matters for X2 comparability (tokens, tool calls, authorship), not for code correctness.

notes: Concurrency reviewed: state mutex held across waitid/kill so the exited guard prevents signalling a reaped PID; stop report consumed without WEXITED (never reaps); has_report treats errors as 'something happened' (fail-safe); the signal-hook registry installs SA_RESTART; SIGCONT arriving before spawn is buffered and is a no-op. K6a holds: the launcher only stops its own PID and only continues the child PID, and it never calls tcsetpgrp. K16 holds: /dev/tty is opened O_NOCTTY|O_NONBLOCK and only queried. Tests use plain exec as a control in a fresh shell for every scenario, cover bash and zsh, and have red proofs against the baseline. They are timing-based but have generous bounds.
